title: Anisotropic wavevector-dependent damping of thickness-quantized magnons
authors: Tamara Azevedo, Rostyslav O. Serha, Yannik Kunz, Matthias R. Schweizer, Vitaliy I. Vasyuchka, Mathias Weiler, Andrii V. Chumak, Burkard Hillebrands, Mikhail Kostylev, Alexander A. Serga
abstract: Magnon damping is a key factor governing spin-wave transport and nonlinear dynamics of multimode magnon systems. However, many descriptions rely on the assumption of an effective mode-independent parameter, which can mask wavelength-dependent relaxation processes that depend on propagation geometry and mode profile. Here, we employ high-resolution parametric-instability spectroscopy to probe thickness-quantized spin waves with wavelengths down to about a hundred nanometers in micrometer-thick yttrium iron garnet films. The instability threshold exhibits a regular sawtooth dependence on the magnetic field, arising from switching between discrete thickness modes. Comparison with dipole--exchange theory reveals anisotropic wavevector-dependent damping that increases with mode number and depends differently on the in-plane and out-of-plane wavevector components.
summary: This work investigates magnon damping in thin YIG films by measuring the parametric instability threshold. The authors demonstrate that damping is not a simple, mode-independent constant but depends anisotropically on the spin-wave wavevector components. This finding is crucial for accurately modeling spin-wave transport and nonlinear dynamics in confined magnetic structures.
main_problem: To overcome the limitation of describing magnon damping using a single, effective, mode-independent parameter, which can mask wavelength-dependent relaxation processes.
main_result: The study reveals anisotropic wavevector-dependent damping in thickness-quantized magnons, evidenced by a linear dependence of the damping loss parameter on the in-plane wavevector component.
method: High-resolution parametric-instability spectroscopy is used to probe the threshold of parametric instability in YIG films, which is then analyzed using dipole-exchange theory.
model_or_system: The physical system is spin waves in micrometer-thick yttrium iron garnet (YIG) films, where the wavevector is quantized in the out-of-plane direction ($k_{oop}$) and varies continuously in the in-plane direction ($k_{ip}$).
key_observables: The parametric instability threshold power ($P_{thr}$) and the extracted magnetic-loss parameter ($\Delta H(n, k_{ip})$).
important_parameters: Film thickness ($d$), magnetic field ($\mu_0H$), in-plane wavevector ($k_{ip}$), and thickness-mode index ($n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed sawtooth structure is due to mode switching and that the loss parameter can be locally extracted from the threshold power dependence.
figures_summary: Figures show the characteristic sawtooth dependence of the instability threshold on the magnetic field, and comparisons between theoretical models using mode-independent versus wavevector-dependent damping successfully reproduce the observed modulation.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental technique using parametric instability spectroscopy to measure magnon damping. It then compares results obtained using simplified, mode-independent damping models against those derived from the full wavevector-dependent theory, demonstrating the necessity of anisotropy.
why_interesting: The detailed characterization of wavevector-dependent damping mechanisms in magnons provides a concrete example of how geometric confinement and anisotropy modify fundamental material parameters, which is relevant for understanding energy dissipation in quantum magnetic systems.
